team offense.bio:
Team Offense was an eight-man Toronto hip-hop crew: Aristo, Cali Snipes, Sese (now recording as Sayzee), Littles The General, Choice, Ceaza Leon, El Niño and Menace. With East Coast roots inside a Toronto crew (Littles was born in Nova Scotia), they moved as a unit on records and on the HipHopCanada message boards. In 2006 they fired the first shot in Drake's first official rap beef, taking on Drake and his crew the Wise Guys with the diss record "Publicity Stunt," a fight that played out on the boards, on wax and on Toronto radio. The crew never released a group tape under the Team Offense name; its members' work lives under their own names, from Littles' and Syph's Perfect Strangers to Sese and Ceaza Leon's The Write Brothers and Sayzee's long-running YFRWN series. Littles The General was killed in Georgetown, Ontario, in October 2019.

Members: Aristo · Cali Snipes · Sayzee (as Sese) · Littles The General · Choice · Ceaza Leon · El Niño · Menace

wise guys.bio:
The Wise Guys were the Toronto crew Drake ran with at the start of his career: Bishop Brigante, Ken Masters, Jonny Roxx, Young Tony (also known as Hush), JD Era and Drake. In 2006 they stood across from Team Offense in what became Drake's first official rap beef, answering the "Publicity Stunt" diss first with Drake's solo reply "Goodnight & Goodluck" and then as a full unit on the Boi-1da-produced "Good Riddance," with Drake closing the record. HipHopCanada's history of the era calls it arguably Drake's first win against his early critics. The conflict was short-lived and eventually squashed.

Members: Bishop Brigante · Ken Masters · Jonny Roxx · Young Tony (Hush) · JD Era · Drake

littles the general.bio: Littles The General was the recording name of Ryan Lorde, a Nova Scotia-born MC who became a central voice of Toronto crew Team Offense. He led the crew's "Publicity Stunt" diss — recorded with Quake Matthews and Greedy — that opened Drake's first official rap beef in 2006, and carried the same title on his own Publicity Stunt project, which included "Streets Is War" featuring JC and Cali Snipes. He later teamed with Syph for the Perfect Strangers mixtape and moved into management and promotion, working with artists including Syph and Dutch Revz. Littles was killed in Georgetown, Ontario, in October 2019, at 36. HipHopCanada's obituary for him recalls, fittingly, his place in Drake's first official rap beef.

cali snipes.bio: Cali Snipes is a Toronto MC and member of Team Offense, the crew that took on Drake and the Wise Guys in 2006. His signature record is the Rich Kidd-produced single "Money 2 Burn," released with a video directed by The Sharpshooter; its remix brought in Famous, Mayhem Morearty, Luu Breeze, Tona and Richie Sosa. He also recorded "The Streets" with Aristo and Ceaza Leon, appeared on Littles The General's "Streets Is War," guested on Sese's first YFRWN tape in 2010, and followed with his own U.M.C.S. (Unauthorized Music of Cali Snipes) project in 2011.

ceaza leon.bio: Ceaza Leon is a Toronto rapper and producer, born October 17, 1984, and a member of Team Offense. Behind the boards he produced for St. Laz, Aristo, Hustlemann, The Corps and The Offense itself, and he was a founding member of Battleground Entertainment. In 2010 he teamed with Scorsese — the name Sese recorded under before Sayzee — as The Write Brothers; their mixtape of the same name was hosted by DJ Vlad and DJ 2Nice, presented by Team Offense, and launched with the single "Bang." He is also a member of The Commitee, alongside El Niño, Choice and Rev.

choice.bio:
Choice is a Toronto MC documented as a member of Team Offense, the eight-man crew behind the 2006 "Publicity Stunt" diss that opened Drake's first official rap beef. He is also named as a member of The Commitee, the group he shared with fellow Team Offense members Ceaza Leon and El Niño, and Rev. Beyond those crew records, very little of his catalogue or biography survives in the sources available.

This profile is currently under research — check back later as we piece together the blog-era record.

el niño.bio:
El Niño is a Toronto MC documented as a member of Team Offense, the crew that fired the first shot in Drake's first official rap beef in 2006. He is also named as a member of The Commitee, alongside Ceaza Leon, Choice and Rev, and he appears with Cali Snipes on "The Future," preserved in Mega City Hip Hop's audio archive. Little else from his catalogue has survived the blog era in the sources available.

This profile is currently under research — check back later as we piece together the blog-era record.

menace.bio:
Menace is a Toronto MC documented as a member of Team Offense, the eight-man crew behind the 2006 "Publicity Stunt" diss that opened Drake's first official rap beef, and he is credited as a featured artist on Littles The General's Publicity Stunt project. No solo catalogue under his name has surfaced in the sources available.

This profile is currently under research — check back later as we piece together the blog-era record.

ken masters.bio: Ken Masters is a Toronto MC and member of the Wise Guys, the crew Drake ran with at the start of his career. He takes the second verse on "Good Riddance," the Boi-1da-produced group diss that answered Team Offense in 2006. Masters also ran the Ken Masters House blog, where in April 2007 he published an interview with Drake that asked him directly about the Aristo beef — one of the few surviving first-person documents of the era. A 2010 blog profile credited him with opening arena shows for Young Buck, Mario and Inspectah Deck, and with a west coast tour alongside The Game; his remake of Jay Electronica's "Exhibit A" circulated through blogs the same year.

jonny roxx.bio: Jonny Roxx is the recording name of Alonzo Thornhill, a Toronto artist and member of the Wise Guys, with a verse on the crew's 2006 diss record "Good Riddance." He released a mixtape under the name in 2008, including the track "Hands Wet," before stepping away from recording. Thornhill went on to build a second career in fitness as a performance coach — co-founder of Push Pounds Sports Medicine — and is best known today as Drake's personal trainer, travelling with him on tour.

young tony.bio:
Young Tony is a Toronto MC and member of the Wise Guys, the crew Drake ran with at the start of his career. He has a verse on "Good Riddance," the Boi-1da-produced group diss that answered Team Offense in 2006. Unlike most of the crew, he stayed in Drake's orbit after the beef era, becoming known as Hush — Exclaim's Drake timeline identifies him as "Young Tony (aka OVO Hush)." Little solo material from his recording years survives in the sources available.

This profile is currently under research — check back later as we piece together the blog-era record.
